output.summary: A columnar cactus endemic to Mexico, Indian comb forms a tall, many-branched tree. Its white flowers open in the evening and close by midday, while its golden-spined fruits split when ripe to reveal red, juicy pulp and black seeds.
output.edibilityNote: Fruit is eaten raw or cooked and made into syrup, preserves, jam or wine; the Mayo historically made foods from ground seeds and cornmeal.
